adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.6. No events are scheduled. The price is 6.2% above regular, which historically correlates with lower demand: past price hikes to 12.03 saw median sales drop to 13.5 (x0.73 vs baseline). The heatwave (38°C) is a new demand driver; similar extreme heat in prior years (2023, 2024) saw sales spike 32% vs baseline, with noise-adjusted effect x1.15. The classical model ignores price and weather. Combining the price downside and heatwave upside, the net effect is uncertain. Shrink toward 1.0 due to weak evidence (one past heat event, price change not previously tested).

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.6 | 5%-95%: 2.9 - 39.3 | 10%-90%: 6.9 - 34.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
